A new State Government plan to bypass local planning laws and allow for greater density around three western suburbs train stations will go before WA’s peak planning body in a confidential meeting.

The Western Australian Planning Commission met Wednesday to consider the draft station precincts improvement plan, covering nine metropolitan train station precincts including Cottesloe, Mosman Park and Swanbourne.

The meeting, which was held behind closed doors, will assess the draft scheme sets a broader vision and objectives to guide development around the precincts.

Planning Minister John Carey announced the station precinct initiative last year as part of the Cook Government’s push to boost housing supply and encourage higher-density development around public transport hubs.

Under the proposal, the WAPC would ultimately gain the power to set zoning, density and development standards and determine future development applications within the precincts.

Wednesday’s meeting will not decide on those controls, but rather whether the commission should recommend the draft scheme to the minister for approval — the first step required before a future scheme can be prepared.

Western suburbs councils have previously raised their concerns about the scheme. They argue it could override their own planning strategies and see years of consultation cast aside.

Ahead of the meeting, Cottesloe, Mosman Park and Peppermint Grove local governments submitted deputations, all advocating for the improvement scheme to incorporate the local planning frameworks.

Cottesloe’s written submission reiterated that it has already spent “considerable funding and resources” to develop and adopt its precinct structure plan.

“The Cottesloe Village precinct structure plan and the town’s nearly completed draft local planning strategy clearly demonstrates how the town was to easily meet the State Government’s infill targets at the town’s train stations,” the statement read.

When announcing the scheme last year, Mr Carey criticised Cottesloe’s local planning framework, claiming it did not encompass a broad enough area.

“While some local governments have taken steps to update planning frameworks around train stations, progress has been slow, and in many cases, density settings are far too low,” he said.

“The Cottesloe council has not been ambitious enough in relation to the density that could occur at the train station.

“If WAPC endorses the blueprint, the recommendation will be referred to Mr Carey, who will make a final decision on whether to approve the improvement plan.”
